ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows the outer outline of a large equilateral triangle, with one unshaded small equilateral triangle cut off at each of the three corners: one at the top, one at the lower left corner, and one at the lower right corner. The remaining central gray region is an irregular hexagon; each cut-off small triangle shares a new cut edge with the gray hexagon. Reasoning: Let the side lengths of the three cut-off equilateral triangles be a, b, and c respectively. The perimeter of the original large equilateral triangle is 60 cm, and the perimeter of the hexagon formed after cutting off the three corners is 40 cm. When a corner triangle of side length x is cut off, two outer edges of length x are lost from the original boundary, but one cut edge of length x is newly added, so the total perimeter decreases by x. Therefore the total decrease is 60 - 40 = 20 cm, that is, a + b + c = 20 cm. The sum of the perimeters of the three cut-off equilateral triangles is 3a + 3b + 3c = 3(a + b + c) = 3 × 20 = 60 cm.
